# Gospel of Thomas, Saying 74 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Nag Hammadi Codex II, p. 48 | **Source Image:** source-texts/coptic/GTH_074_page_001.jpg

---

## Saying 74

**1** He said: "Lord, there are many around the drinking-trough, but there is nothing in the well."

---

**Consensus Notes (SOPHIA):**

**Text:** One of the most enigmatic sayings in Thomas. The crowd gathers at the watering-place but the source is empty.

**"Drinking-trough"** — EMET preserved over "cistern" (LOGOS) — emphasizes the gathering-to-drink function. PNEUMA's "watering-place" is acceptable but loses the vessel specificity.

**"Nothing in the well"** — "nothing in" preserves the literal Coptic construction; PNEUMA's "empty" is interpretively equivalent but less literal.

**Theological Note:** Interpretations include: (1) many follow religion outwardly but find no inner substance; (2) the crowd seeks Jesus but is not spiritually prepared to receive him; (3) there are many seeking but few true finders (cf. Saying 2). The saying is unique to Thomas.
